mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for a backyard sauna in Burlington?

acceptedAnswer.text: An accessory building over 10 m² typically needs a building permit, zoning setbacks apply, and the electrical connection needs an ESA permit. In the Niagara Escarpment Plan area, a Niagara Escarpment Commission permit may also be needed. We check before you order.

mainEntity.name: I'm in Kilbride. Can I have a wood-burning sauna?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, on our larger saunas and barrels. Rural escarpment properties may need extra approvals, and you should check your insurer's requirements for wood stoves.

mainEntity.name: What base does a sauna need?

acceptedAnswer.text: A level gravel pad or concrete slab. We recommend which suits your yard and soil.

mainEntity.name: How much does delivery and installation cost in Burlington?

acceptedAnswer.text: Delivery and installation is $1,750 anywhere in Ontario, including Burlington. Delivery only is $450. HST is shown separately on every quote.

mainEntity.name: What heater size does my sauna need?

acceptedAnswer.text: We size every heater to the sauna's interior volume plus extra for glass. None of our saunas take less than a 6 kW heater; larger models use 9 to 10.5 kW electric or a wood stove where there's room for its clearances.
